newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate inches up 10 bps to 11.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate inches up 10 bps to 11.1 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate inched up 10 basis points to 11.1 percent on Monday amid short supply of kuna funds, which left some bank borrowers empty handed.
Trade totalled 74.5 million kuna, of which 32.5 million in old borrowings was rolled over by lenders at mixed rates.
The weighted interbank call money rate added 10 basis points to 10.1 percent after some banks reverted to the 10.5-percent price due to stronger demand.
They charged 11-13 percent for one-week loans, 13 for two-weeks and 15 percent for one-month placements.
Insurers granted seven-day kuna at an unchanged 9.0 percent and 30-day funds at 15 percent.

The central bank's kuna midrates for Tuesday which reflect the sell rates of the leading banks also ended mixed, easing to 6.1893 against the dollar and firming to 3.5698 versus the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
